Commentary.Commentary: 272 is the target then for Zimbabwe. Going by their batting in South Africa, one will not be too hopeful of a fight. But as a fan, we certainly hope that we get a contest.

Jarvis says that he is personally happy with how he want but looking from the team's perspective, he says that he would have been happier had they restricted Bangladesh to 220 or beyond. Admits that in the middle phase, they got 3-4 quick wickets and at that point, they felt they could restrict Bangladesh to 220 but credits Imrul Kayes for his fantastic knock. Is still hopeful of a win but feels at least 2 batsmen need to get a big score.

'Well begun is half done', goes the saying. Zimbabwe started really well but unfortunately they could not finish it off. They had the opportunity to keep the hosts under 200 but they have conceded much more. Kyle Jarvis was at his best, getting his maiden ODI 4-fer while Chatara got some free wickets towards the end, finishing with 3. Here is Jarvis having a chat with Athar Ali Khan.

The home side needed someone to hang around with Imrul Kayes and Mohammad Saifuddin was chosen as that guy. The former had to cut down his attacking strokes and the run rate dropped down. However, the duo then started to attack from the 35th over. From there, the visitor simply could not get back. The pair added a wonderful 129 for the 7th wicket with the last 15 overs going for 114 runs.

After electing to bat on a sluggish surface, the hosts struggled big time. They could not quite gauge  the surface and lost their wickets cheaply. The middle order then staged a recovery but Jarvis' second spell broke their back. They lost 3 wickets for 2 runs in the space of 15 balls and at that stage, it seemed like they will fold up for 175 or less. But Bangladesh had other ideas.
Tremendous recovery from Bangladesh. That will be an understatement. Down in the dumps at 139/6, a 127-run stand for the 7th wicket has completely turned the game around.
A full toss to end the innings, the skipper swings hard but only times it towards mid-wicket. Just a single. BANGLADESH END ON 271/8!
Outside off, closer than the previous one, MM slashes but misses again.
Full and wide outside off, Mashrafe swings hard but cannot reach it. He looks at the umpire hoping for a wide call but does not get it. The ball came back in at the last moment.
Outside off, chipped down to long off for a run.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.

OUT! A wicket on the first ball. A full toss outside off, Saifuddin looks to hit it over the top but cannot quite clear the man at long off. Brandon Mavuta takes it easily at the ropes and that ends Saifuddin's fine knock. Two wickets in quick succession for Zimbabwe but they have come 120 runs too late.
Tendai Chatara to bowl the final over. 9-1-51-2 so far. Might see a lot of bat swinging in this over.

A short ball, down the leg side, Mortaza looks to tuck it fine but cannot get it past Brendan Taylor who dives to his left to stop it. Great finish from Jarvis - 4 runs and a wicket to end with figures of 9-1-37-4.
HALF CENTURY FOR SAIFUDDIN! His first in ODIs. How well has he played? Incredibly well. Gets to his half century with a gentle push towards long on.
Skipper Mashrafe Mortaza is the new man in, for the finishing duties.

A length ball outside off, Kayes, backing away, reaches out to hit it over cover but finds Peter Moor running to his right to take that catch near the boundary. Jarvis is pumped up with his maiden 4-fer in ODIs. Kayes is asked to wait as the umpires want to check the no ball. But Jarvis is fine as per the replays. All the Zimbabwe players now walk across to Imrul and shake his hand. Terrific knock.
Pushes this towards mid on and scampers through.
A yorker outside off, Imrul backs away and guides it towards third man for a run.
Full and outside off, hit hard towards long off for a single.
A short ball to end the over, fended to the leg side for a run. 12 from this over, 48 from the last 3!
A yorker now, squeezed through the covers for a single.

NOT OUT. Cannot exactly say what would have been going through the third umpire's mind. To the first look via the naked eye, it seemed out. Straight into the fielder's hands. It was a length ball outside off and Saifuddin guided it straight to Craig Ervine at first slip. The fielder took it low and then claimed the catch. However, the umpire was not sure and took it upstairs. Now, the second look. It still seems out - right into the palms. But then, when they try to zoom, it seems like we are watching a pixellated movie. In such films, the more you zoom, the blurred they become. The replays are zoomed in, ultrazoomed, then zoomed out but eventually given NOT OUT.

Is that wicket number 7? Saifuddin has guided it towards first slip and Craig Ervine is claiming the catch. Umpire Dharmasena though has shaken his head but then referred it upstairs. The soft signal is NOT OUT.

OUT! Two wickets in the over! Jarvis has brought Zimbabwe firing back into this contest. But a debatable decision. On a length outside off, Mahmudullah looks to defend but at the last moment, seems to be withdrawing his bat. There is a noise as the ball goes past and Jarvis appeals, with the umpire raising his finger. Mahmudullah immediately reviews and here comes the tricky part. Snickometer shows a spike when the ball passes the bat. But if you compare it with the sideways angle, it seems like the ball has passed the bat and the sound is of the bat hitting the pad. However, the benefit of doubt is given to the bowler, perhaps because the on-field umpire gave it out. Big, big decision. Could be the turning point in this game.

Massive wicket for Zimbabwe. The Kayes-Rahim stand was just developing big proportions and it has been broken just when it was about to touch 50. The bowling has been more or less disciplined, but on a pitch which seems to be aiding turn, they need to bowl Bangladesh out under 200. Or restrict them. Rahim could have played for a long time on this type of a wicket. Here is MOHAMMAD MITHUN.

There was a noise as the ball went past the bat and Brendan Taylor immediately went up on the sound. Umpire Dharmasena though, shook his head. Taylor convinced his skipper to for the review and Snickometer showed a big deflection when the ball went past the glove. OUT! The stand is broken one short of 50.
Now, now, now.... is Rahim out? Taylor is confident that he has caught him down the leg side. Which keeper will get the umpire's verdict in his favour? Review taken by Zimbabwe.

OUT! What a catch! The debutant has come and gone. On a length outside off, Mahmud looks to defend but suddenly the ball bounces sharply and he has nowhere to go. Limply hangs his bat, tries to fend but the ball takes the outside edge. It flies over the slip cordon but Brendan Taylor leaps to his left, sticks out his glove and voila! it sticks!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Banged in short, pulled towards deep square leg for a single.
In comes the debutant, Fazle Mahmud.

OUT! Caught this time! Full and outside off, Das jumps down the track, aims to go over the top but the slow pitch does not allow the ball to come onto the bat properly. It takes the toe and and lobs wide of mid off. Cephas Zhuwao gets across to his left and takes a nice tumbling catch.

DROPPED, FOUR! Ohhh... schoolboy stuff. Brandon Mavuta has put down a sitter. A length ball on middle and leg, Kayes swings this over square leg. It goes straight to the man at the ropes, Mavuta, who just puts it down. Then concedes a boundary too.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
The batsman gets a bottom edge of the bat on that one.
The batsman has lofted that over mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
A short ball outside off, pulled straight to mid on. Almost hit it straight to him.
Action replay! Think the hamstring is gone. He comes jogging in but even before he can reach the umpire, he pulls out.  AND JARVIS IS WALKING OFF. Donald Tiripano to bowl from Jarvis' end.
Issues for Jarvis. He comes running in but then aborts his runup at the last moment. Has he pulled up his hamstring? He is continuing though...
Full and outside off, a slash and a miss.
A short ball, rises steeply, Imrul looks to fend at it but the ball hits his gloves and drops down.
Short and outside off, played straight to point again.
Outside off, played straight to point.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, Kayes slashes hard but misses.

NOT OUT! Looks like Raza has dropped one. Full and outside off, Das bludgeoned it through the off side. It went straight to Raza at cover who took it, but then the ball bobbed out of his hands. Then he got up and signalled to the third  umpire. Replays show that the ball fell down. Good sportsmanship from Raza but what a reprieve for Das.
Is that out? Das has hit a powerful cover drive. Sikandar Raza has taken the catch but he himself said that he is not sure. Wants to refer it upstairs. The soft signal is OUT.
Outside off, left alone. That came back in a long way...
A short ball outside off, Das looks to pull but misses.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full and outside off, angled away, Imrul looks to open the face of the bat and run it towards third man but gets an outside edge past second slip. A single taken.
NEARLY! On a length outside off, Kayes looked to push at it but the ball got stuck on the surface. Took the inside edge and hit him on the pads, narrowly missing the stumps.
On middle and leg, tucked towards square leg for a run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Full and outside off, Kayes leans and lofts it over cover for the first boundary of the match.
The batsman has worked it off his pads behind square. They pick up a single.
WIDE. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Liton was gone for all money. Outside off, Das tapped it towards point and set off for a single. Kayes responded but then changed his mind. Liton was far too down the track to even think of going back. He gave up. Sean Williams had plenty of time to have a shy at the striker's end but missed.
Outside off, played towards point.
Tendai Chatara to bowl with the second new ball.
Full and on middle, Imrul is squared up and gets a leading edge towards mid off. Good opening over from Jarvis.
Stays back and blocks again.
Around off, solidly defended.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Landed outside off, dabbed towards third man for a single. Bangladesh are away.
On a length outside off, pushed towards cover.
The players are out in the middle. Liton Das and Imrul Kayes will open the batting for the home side. Kyle Jarvis to bowl with the first new ball. Das to face. Here we go!
TOSS - BANGLADESH HAVE WON THE TOSS AND ELECTED TO BAT.

We are all set for the home season of Bangladesh to get underway. Zimbabwe are the challenge in front of them - slated to play 3 ODIs and 2 Tests. The home side, no doubt, will be the favourites to win but Zimbabwe can perhaps play with more freedom and cause a surprise.
